subject: math

entries: y = a·f(x) + d: stretch the height, then lift the graph: multiplying by a stretches every y-coordinate by a factor of a, and adding d lifts the whole graph by d.
slots.label: Stretch the height, then lift the graph
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: y = f(bx + c): read it as f(b(x + c/b)): factor out b so the shift c/b and the squeeze by b can each be read honestly.
slots.label: Factor out b inside the brackets
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Reciprocal functions: the asymptotes run the show: as x grows the curve flattens onto the horizontal asymptote, and as x approaches the vertical asymptote the curve shoots up it and the sign flips across it.
slots.label: Reciprocal functions: the asymptotes run the show
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The +c trap: inside the brackets means shift LEFT: f(x + 3) is zero where x = -3, to the left of the original root, so the whole graph sits 3 units further left.
slots.label: The +c trap: inside means shift left
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A rule that assigns exactly one output to each input: f(x) names the output of the rule f at the input x, and the graph of y = f(x) plots every input against its output.
slots.label: Function
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A change to the equation of a graph that moves or resizes it in a predictable way: changes outside f act vertically, and changes inside f act horizontally and in the opposite direction to the sign.
slots.label: Transformation
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A transformation that scales distances from an axis by a fixed factor: y = a·f(x) stretches heights by a factor of a, while y = f(bx) squeezes widths by a factor of b.
slots.label: Stretch
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A transformation that shifts the whole graph without changing its shape: + d outside f lifts the graph by d, while + c inside the brackets shifts it left by c.
slots.label: Translation
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A function built from one divided by an expression, such as y = 1/x: its graph comes in separate branches divided by its vertical asymptote.
slots.label: Reciprocal function
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A line that a curve approaches ever more closely but never touches: y = 1/x has the vertical asymptote x = 0 and the horizontal asymptote y = 0.
slots.label: Asymptote
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: JC H2 functions and graphs: transformations, reciprocal functions, asymptote behaviour
